title.narrative: Partnership in Education and Skills for Inclusive Green Growth (PESIG)

description.narrative:
This proposed Action seeks to contribute to equitably enhance the education and skills base among Laos¿ youth responding to labour market needs of a green and digitalised economy, while taking into account gender-specific issues and decent work standards, in full alignment with the Lao Government and European Partners¿ development agendas.

The Overall Objective (Impact) of this action is to support the priority policy objectives of the ESSDP 2021-2025, including the TVET Development Plan 2021-2025, and the European Joint Programming Strategy 2021-2025 as to improve qualifications and skills of Laos¿ youth responding to labour market needs of a green and digitalised economy

The Specific(s) Objective(s) (Outcomes) of this action are to:

1. Improve equitable access and learning outcomes of general education (particularly related to gender equality, and in rural and remote areas) - [ESSDP High-level Outcomes 1, 2 & 3]

2. Enhance effectiveness of TVET subsector equipping graduates with relevant skills responding to the labour market and the needs of a green and digitalised economy - [ESSDP High-level Outcome 5]

3. Improve education sector performance and reduce disparities - [ESSDP High-level Outcomes 3, 6 &7]

As one of the biggest development partners and budget support providers for the education sector, and co-chair of the education sector working group, the EU has been an influential actor in the education reform agenda. As such, the proposed action will continue to place the EU at the heart of it, including on equitable access (especially in remote areas with ethnic minorities), teaching/learning quality, and sector governance/financing. In addition, the stronger emphasis on TVET as Team Europe, will raise the political nature of EU support in this sub-sector, by laying the foundations for the planned interventions in Agriculture & forestry, and trade & private sector development under priority area 1 of the MIP and by linking it to the overarching MIP objective to strengthen EU¿s trade and investment in Lao PDR, especially in green sectors. Furthermore, the EU intends to increase emphasis on education financing and spending efficiency (notably through the full operationalisation of the Education Planning and Budget Committee and the Teacher Allocation Committee, and the implementation of the recommendations of the ongoing Education Public Expenditure Review). These activities will closely involvee relevant Ministries and national/provincial assemblies and further strengthening the political aspect of our support. The provision of BS will also provide an opportunity for policy dialogue on macroeconomic policies, PFM reforms, and budget transparency in relation to the BS assessment criteria, accompanied by technical support under another EU-funded project to support PFM reforms

description.narrative: Enhance effectiveness of TVET subsector equipping graduates with relevants skills responding to the labour makret and the needs of a green and digitalised economy (ESSDP Highlevel Outcome 5)

title.narrative: Improving the quality and relevance of programmes in public TVET institutions through application of Competency Based Training (CBT) curriculum and Dual Cooperative Training (DCT) curriculum

description.narrative: The purpose of this indicator is to assess the progress of TVET institutions in improving the quality and relevance of programmes (courses); namely the demandoriented national curriculum CompetencyBased Training (CBT) and the Dual Cooperative Training (DCT) curriculum organised by TVET institutions in cooperation with the private sector. Courses are intended to match the local socioeconomic needs in priority economic sectors (e.g. Agroforestry, Agribusiness, Tourism/Hospitality, Energy), and with priority in disadvantaged districts (DD). Gender issues are routinely mainstreamed in TVET curricula and related materials.

title.narrative: Implementation of the Lao Qualifications Framework (LQF) for TVET through development of new Occupational Standards in priority trades and sectors.

description.narrative: The purpose of this indicator is to assess progress in the implementation of the LQF as a mechanism for promoting and overseeing the development of a highquality vocational qualification system that responds to the needs of labour market, including in the fields of green and digitalised economy. Occupational Standards (OS) are developed by DTVET in cooperation with Trade Working Groups (TWGs) as a basis for development of new qualifications. The Occupational Standards are linked to the learning outcomes specified in the LQF TVET qualifications levels 15.

comment.narrative: Fourteen 14 Occupational Standards OS are reported by MoES to be approved by MoES decree in five sectors as of 082022
Five new Occupational Standards OS approved by MoES Decrees from 01072024 to 30062025.Sources of verification Occupational Standards decrees DTVET and TWG reports.

title.narrative: Development of financing mechanisms for improved resourcing of TVET through the establishment of a TVET Development Fund (TDF)

description.narrative: This indicator will assess measures implemented by the MoES and other relevant Ministries (Ministry of Finance in particular), in partnership with the private sector, to diversify the sources of funding for TVET institutions through the TVET Development Fund (TDF).

comment.narrative: The TDF has been created by the TVET Law but is not yet operational while waiting for the approval of a new decree introducing mechanisms for private sector funding. Existing TVET institutions are currently financed either by the State budget with Development Partners DP support or by private funding initiatives corporate training centres or LNCCI pilot initiatives with DP support e.g. KfWVEFF project.Sources of verification MoESDTVET reports TVET Law TVETDP projects reports
At least LAK 4 billion allocated from the 2025 MoES budget to the TDF for the development of TVET institutionsSources of verification MoES annual budget 2025 DGTVET reports

The Prime Ministerial Decree on the TDF No. 194 was approved on 19 April 2023. This achieves part of the indicator target for both 2023 and 2024.However TDF financial management regulations are not part of the TDF decree and they are not the responsibility of and will not be approved by the Prime Ministers Office.MoES will develop TDF Guidelines that will include financial management regulations during the second half of 2023 to be approved by MoES.The indicator target is not achieved and the specific condition has not been met

title.narrative: Specific Objective 3

description.narrative: Improve education sector performance and reduce disparities

title.narrative: Percentage of districts achieving the Parity Index of primary teacher allocation at R2 0.8

description.narrative: The purpose of this indicator is to measure progress in improving the efficiency and equity of primary teacher distribution within districts. More specifically the indicator measures progress in improving the allocation of teachers within districts, to address issues of over and under supply at the school level. The indicator has been successfully used in the previous budget support, with technical assistance to develop tools and build capacity at the district level for allocating teachers more effectively.

comment.narrative: 87 districts achieved the Parity Index of primary teacher allocation at R2 0.8 in 202122 R2 1 indicates perfect equity
104 districts achieving the Parity Index of primary teacher allocation at R2 0.8 in 202324

91 districts have achieved the Parity Index of primary teacher allocation at R2 0.8 in 202223The indicator target is partially achieved and the specific condition has been partially met translating to a 50 disbursement.

description.narrative: Improve education sector performance and reduce disparities

title.narrative: ESSDP Financing Plan, Annual Costed Sector Plans and draft budget plans are reviewed by the Planning and Budgeting Committee to ensure consistency with ESSDP expenditure priorities

description.narrative: The purpose of this indicator is to measure performance of the Planning and Budgeting Committee (PBC) in implementing its key functions related to strengthening linkages between strategic planning and budgeting, and therefore contributing to improved prioritisation of resources.

comment.narrative: The MoES PBC was established in 2017 and its mandate updated in 2021 but it has not yet implemented its function as the platform for MoES interdepartmental budget discussions.
Target to be defined through an exchange of letter following the approval of the Education Public Expenditure and Institutional Review PEIR

title.narrative: Specific objectives 1

description.narrative: Improve equitable access and learning outcomes of general education (particularly related to gender equality, and in rural and remote areas) ESSDP High level Outcome 1, 2 and 3

title.narrative: Percentage of primary shcool grade 1 entrants in the 40 disadvantage districts having attended ECE in the previous year disaggregated by gender

description.narrative: The purpose of this indicator is to measure progress in the expansion of ECE in disadvantaged areas, particularly at the immediate preprimary level, as a key factor in promoting school readiness. Attendance at the preprimary level is critical in increasing enrolment, improving retention, and reducing repetition in primary education. Providing an opportunity for children to start to learn the Lao language in ECE (in predominantly nonLao speaking areas that are generally more disadvantaged) can specifically assist with readiness for primary education.

comment.narrative: 59.8 of primary school grade 1 entrants in the 40 DDs in SY 202122 attended ECE in SY 202021
Completion scoring method 1 if achieved totally 0.5 if partially achieved 63.2 0 if not achieved.

description.narrative: Improve equitable access and learning outcomes of general education (particularly related to gender equality, and in rural and remote areas) ESSDP High level Outcome 1, 2 and 3

title.narrative: Establishment and implementation of a system for a continuous Professional Development (CPD) for teachers

description.narrative: The purpose of this indicator is to measure progress in the MoES development and implementation of a systemic approach to improving the quality and delivery of CPD for ECE and primary education teachers. This will increase the number of knowledgeable and competent teachers (and school principals) resulting in improved teaching, to better facilitate ECE and primary students learning. Increases in government funding for CPD will be important given its low levels and a history of dependency on development partners for funding CPD. In this respect the indicator will promote sustainability.

MoES 2025 budget for ECE and primary education teacher CPD increased to a minimum of LAK 10.5 billion

description.narrative: The purpose of the indicator is to assess progress in improving equity in the provision of SBGs, through a revised funding formula addressing the comparatively higher costs per student incurred in smaller schools and in more disadvantaged areas.In addition, in the context of a significant decline in the SBG budget from 2019 to 2023 (see baseline), the indicator will support gradual increases in the SBG budget. title.narrative: School Block Grand formula is reviewed and revised to improve equity in respect to school size (year one) followed by increases in MoES SBG budget ad tranfer according to the new formula and guidelines

description.narrative: The purpose of the indicator is to assess progress in improving equity in the provision of SBGs, through a revised funding formula addressing the comparatively higher costs per student incurred in smaller schools and in more disadvantaged areas.In addition, in the context of a significant decline in the SBG budget from 2019 to 2023 (see baseline), the indicator will support gradual increases in the SBG budget. The indicator will also support timely and full payment to schools according to SBG guidelines.

title.narrative: UNESCO Institute for Statistics Youth literacy rate

description.narrative: SDG Indicator 4.6.2: The youth literacy rate is defined by the percentage of the population aged 15 to 24 years that can read and write. It is typically measured according to the ability to comprehend a short simple statement on everyday life. Generally, literacy also encompasses numeracy, and measurement may incorporate a simple assessment of arithmetic ability. The literacy rate and number of literates should be distinguished from functional literacy, a more comprehensive measure of literacy assessed on a continuum in which multiple proficiency levels can be determined.
